To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the autophosphorylated state of CaMKII in the muscle is regulated in a frequency and muscle-type specific manner and that this regulation is not predicted by the computational model.
CaMKII isoform specificity of autophosphorylations in muscle is a novel finding and that the autophosphorylated CaMKII isoforme pattern differs between slow and fast muscle types.
the autophosphorylated state of CaMKII in the muscle is regulated in an isotype and muscle type-specific manner.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of calcium/calmodulin dependent protein kinase II (CAMK II) and its isoforms in muscle.
the question how muscle type-specific differences in CaMKII isoform expression contribute to the specificity in calcium sensing and excitation-transduction coupling between different muscle types.
the role of CaMKII autoregulation in the specificity of myofibrillar calcium sensing.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
CaMKII isoform specificity in muscle is not fully understood and needs to be further investigated.
CaMKII isoform expression is muscle-type specific but that CaMKII activity is not muscle-type specific.
autophosphorylated CaMKII is a potential candidate for the molecular switch of excitation-activation and excitation-transduction coupling in skeletal muscle.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the muscle type specific autophosphorylated CaMKII content is determined by both the muscle type specific CaMKII content and the muscle type specific calcium dynamics.

muscle type specific autophosphorylations of CaMKII are regulated by the muscle fiber type specific expression of different isoforms and by the muscle type specific properties of the myocellular calcium handling.

CaMKII phosphorylation in skeletal muscle after paced contractions can be regulated in a muscle-type-specific manner, with isoform-specific differences in the time course of the phosphorylation and with the possibility that mitochondrial calcium buffering capacity may be important for the phosphorylation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
CaMKII isoform expression and compartment-specific calcium dynamics are key factors for CaMKII autoregulation after excitation.

the autophosphorylated form of CaMKII (CaMKII-P) is not a simple marker for the activation of CaMKII, and that CaMKII isoform-specific phosphorylation can be regulated in a muscle type-specific fashion.

CaMKII isoform specificity in the autophosphorylated state can be modulated by the type and intensity of excitation, and this specificity may be a mechanism to regulate myocellular calcium sensitivity.
